title: How an Espresso Machine Works in 60 Seconds ☕🔥 #shorts
description:
An espresso machine heats water to just below boiling, then a pump forces it through tightly packed coffee at about 9 bar. In around 25 to 30 seconds that pressure pulls out the oils and flavor and creates the golden crema on top. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#espresso #coffee #howitworks

steps.label: Hook
steps.text: Every espresso shot is pushed through coffee at about *9 bar*. That's nine times the air pressure around you.

steps.label: Boiler
steps.text: First, a *boiler* heats water to about *93 degrees*, just below boiling.

steps.label: Pump
steps.text: Then a *pump* forces that hot water up to the *group head* under high pressure.

steps.label: Coffee puck
steps.text: Below it, finely ground coffee is packed tight in the *portafilter*, forming a dense *puck*.

steps.label: Extraction
steps.text: The water squeezes through the puck in about *25 to 30 seconds*, pulling out oils and flavor.

steps.label: Crema
steps.text: Pressure also traps *carbon dioxide* in the coffee, which foams up as golden *crema*.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Heat, pressure, *crema*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
